name: Car rental and chauffeur services

problems.words: The same car got booked to two customers
quick_ideas: Keep one booking calendar for the whole fleet, so every booking is checked against it
Let only one person confirm bookings, so clashes are caught.

workzap_build.text: a fleet availability calendar showing every car's bookings, off-hire and returns, which blocks double bookings.

problems.ask_first: Do double bookings usually come from walk-ins and calls, or from website and agent bookings?
problems.free_stops: Calendar rules and handovers are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many bookings sit in messages before reaching the fleet diary, so you see where double booking risk starts.
Give one dispatcher the handover call before any car is promised, so two customers are not offered the same car.

problems.words: Cars come back with scratches the customer says were already there
quick_ideas: Photograph every car at check-out and check-in, so condition is on record
Note fuel and kilometres at both ends, so there's no argument later.

workzap_build.text: Cars would be checked out and back in on a phone, with timed photos, fuel and kilometre readings, signed by the customer.

problems.ask_first: Do these scratch arguments come mostly with short rentals, or with long ones?
problems.free_stops: The inspection steps are in the solution document; liability is for your lawyer.

extra_ideas.text: Compare return notes with pickup notes for each car this week, so disputed scratches are easy to spot early.
Give one staff member the walk round note at every handover, so every scratch is marked before the car leaves.

problems.words: Fines and tolls arrive after the deposit is released
quick_ideas: Note how long fines usually take to appear, so you can see whether your deposit hold matches
Match each fine to its rental by car and time, so you know who it belongs to.

workzap_build.text: fines and tolls matched to the rental by time and car, with a deposit tracker showing hold, release and deductions.

problems.ask_first: How do you find out about fines on your cars today?
problems.free_stops: How matching and deposit rules work is in the solution document; contracts are for your lawyer.

extra_ideas.text: Note which cars bring late fines and tolls most often, so you can see where follow up work keeps returning.
Keep one notebook page per car for post return charges, so late fines and tolls are matched quickly.

problems.words: I don't know which cars are free tomorrow without calling everyone
quick_ideas: List every car with where it is and when it's next free, so you can answer quickly
Update it at each return, so it stays current.

workzap_build.text: a live fleet view of free, booked and off-hire cars by category.

problems.ask_first: Do you mostly need to know which cars are free the same day, or days ahead?
problems.free_stops: What the fleet view shows is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the yard and compare each car's actual spot with today's notes, so you see why tomorrow's availability stays unclear.
Set one fixed evening update for all returns and handovers, so tomorrow's free cars are known without calling everyone.

problems.words: Cars miss services because nobody tracks kilometres
quick_ideas: Write each car's kilometres and next service on one list, so due cars are visible
Check registration and insurance dates at the same time, so a car isn't stuck.

workzap_build.text: a service and renewal scheduler by kilometres and dates, with off-hire alerts.

problems.ask_first: Do cars miss services because kilometres are not noted, or because the workshop slot is never booked?
problems.free_stops: Service intervals and alerts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each car's current odometer with its last service note, so overdue cars are spotted before more bookings land.
Give one person the job of writing kilometres at every return in one notebook, so service timing stops being missed.

problems.words: Chauffeurs come late for airport pickups
quick_ideas: Ask chauffeurs to confirm the evening before each pickup, so gaps are found early
Keep a backup driver on call for early pickups, so one absence doesn't miss a flight.

workzap_build.text: a chauffeur duty roster with pickup confirmations and duty-hour logs.

problems.ask_first: Are late pickups mostly a few chauffeurs, or spread across most of the team?
problems.free_stops: Roster and confirmation rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which airport pickups start late and by how long, so you see whether the issue is certain shifts or routes.
Give one coordinator the evening handover list for next day's airport runs, so late pickups stop slipping between drivers.

problems.words: Corporate bills are made by hand from log sheets
quick_ideas: Log each corporate trip as it happens, so month end isn't a rebuild
Use the same layout for every client, so bills are quicker.

workzap_build.text: corporate bills generated from logged trips, with statements and ageing.

problems.ask_first: Do corporate bills take long because there are many clients, or because trip logs arrive late?
problems.free_stops: Billing and statement set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many trip details are missing from chauffeur log sheets this week, so billing delays can be tied to the real source.
Keep one notebook only for corporate trip details at dispatch, so month end bills are built from one place.

problems.words: Bookings from WhatsApp, calls, website and agents get lost
quick_ideas: Put every booking into one list, whatever the channel, so nothing is missed
Reply to after-hours messages first thing each morning, so they're not forgotten.

workzap_build.text: booking capture from every channel, including after hours, into one list with confirmations.

problems.ask_first: Which channel loses the most bookings: WhatsApp, calls, the website or agents?
problems.free_stops: Channel set-up and replies are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many booking requests wait in different inboxes before being written down, so the loss point becomes visible.
Give one staff member one booking notebook for every channel, so requests stop disappearing between calls, messages and agents.

problems.words: I don't know profit per car after fuel, service and insurance
quick_ideas: Pick a few cars and list what they earned and cost last month, so you see which earn their keep
Go over that with your accountant, so the figures are read correctly.

workzap_build.text: per-car profit and utilisation by car and category, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Do you want profit for the whole fleet, or first for a few key cars?
problems.free_stops: Which costs are included and how is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one car this week, note every refill and workshop visit beside each booking, so hidden running drains on that car show.
Give one staff member one notebook page per car for daily spend notes, so missing cost details stop delaying car-by-car reviews.

never_say: Advice on rental contracts, liability, insurance excess or contesting fines.
Help moving fines to the wrong person, falsifying accident records or avoiding tolls.
Requests for passports, IDs, licences or card details.
Advice on licensing, investors' returns or financing.
After an accident or passenger emergency, anything before pointing to emergency services.

sample_reply.person: Fines keep showing up weeks after we've released the deposit. Any solution for this?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and the first steps are simple.
First, note how long fines usually take to appear, so you can see whether your deposit hold matches.
Second, match each fine to its rental by car and time, so you know who it belongs to.
Here is what Workzap would build: every fine and toll matched to its rental and each deposit tracked from hold to release.

Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
